pass_limit: RESULT: PASS: at the worst corner the hot edge at or under 45 C and the cold edge at or over 0 C (or the cell's own limits from VER-37 if narrower) (fails at 71737ae: 3.9-48.2 C with TH1 10k B4460, TCTR0805F10K0F4460T, and 5.8-44.5 C nominal; at be437f8 1.4-51.5 C with B3950. B 5130 or more passes, its cold edge 6.5 C; no 10k NTC JLC stocks has it: DEC-05)

title: Power latch state table: PWR_EN through the power button SW24, contact resistance, leakage margins

procedure: before any power, put the FPC into the breakout contacts down (assembly.md section 5 step 6); diode-test to find which header pin is panel 1 (LEDA, forward to 2 and 3) and check continuity among panel 11-24 and 34 (GND); record the breakout header pin each panel pin lands on (it must equal 51 minus the FH12 pad number); then wire an ESP32-S3 dev board by the panel's own pin names on its 8080 8-bit bus (1 LEDA, 2-3 LEDK, 7-8 IM0 and IM1 high, 9 IM2 low, 10 RESET, 25-32 DB7-DB0, 35 RD high, 36 WRX, 37 D/CX, 38 CSX low, 39 TE, 40-42 VDDI/VCI); read ID4 (0xD3) with RD driven for the read only; light each cathode pin (LEDK1, LEDK2: three LEDs each) in turn from the bench supply through 47 ohm; then time a full 320 x 480 redraw in RGB565 at 20 MHz and at 25 MHz (twc 40 ns, ili9488.txt:16159) and a battle-text update

title: Production self-test image
procedure: write a self-test image on the generated pin file (VER-149): buttons and the power key; a GPIO neighbour-bridge test whose pair table is generated from design.ESP32 and the module's pin table, marking each pin safe to toggle or not (PWR_HOLD, CHG_OFF, AMP_EN, BL_PWM, the strapping pins IO0, IO3, IO45, IO46, the PSRAM's IO35-IO37), using the external pull's direction where one exists, on USB power only, and cross-checked against hardware/vv/bridges.csv (VER-148); panel ID and fills; backlight; audio tone; ADC; the microSD card's detect, read and write; Wi-Fi scan and RSSI; charger states incl. the 2 Hz fault; the 24-bit shift-register read; no eFuse or flash-encryption writes

title: Per-unit charge-path screen with USB in and no cell
procedure: bringup.md step 1 (to be added) and the production test, before any cell touches the unit: USB from the bench supply at 5.0 V with a 100 mA limit through a USB-C breakout; DMM on TP1 (VBUS), TP2 (VSYS), TP3 (VBAT), TP7 (TS); scope on TP3 for 10 s (U2's battery detection toggles BAT with no cell); clip leads only (DF-114)
pass_limit: TP2 4.30-4.50 V; TP3 peak <= 4.25 V on the scope; TP7 within design_numbers.py tsband's band at the ambient read beside the board; CHG_PG_N low; every unit
needs: USB-C breakout (about $5, 5d) and a clip-lead set (about $8, 2d)

title: Per-unit CV with a load in place of the cell
procedure: a PicoBlade pigtail (on the saver, VER-157) across J2 carrying the CV load: 160 ohm 0.25 W 1% in parallel with a TL431 (TO-92, cathode to anode set to 3.5 V by 10k over 24.9k 1%) in series with 22 ohm 0.25 W 1%; USB in; read TP3 within 60 s. No resistor alone can do it: design_numbers.py cvload computes from SLUS810N (KPRECHG 70-106 A-ohm, ITERM 0.09-0.11 x ICHG) that a resistor must exceed 147.6 ohm to leave pre-charge and stay under 126.7 ohm never to terminate (O-R2). With the TL431 branch the load sits at 3.31 V or more at the smallest pre-charge current (21.0 mA, the branch off) and draws 52 mA or more at 4.16 V (over the largest termination current, 32.8 mA), at every corner cvload checks. Not a 3.3 V zener (too soft) and not three diodes (they conduct at about 2 V)
pass_limit: TP3 4.158-4.242 V; CHG_STAT_N low (still in CV, not terminated); every unit
instrument: handheld DMM, 0.5% + 2 counts; checked against the 4.096 V reference that session
needs: 160 ohm and 22 ohm 0.25 W 1% resistors, a TL431 in TO-92, 10k and 24.9k 1% resistors and a PicoBlade pigtail pair (about $3, LCSC, 7d)

title: Per-unit TS window: TH1 is an NTC and the hot pause works

pass_limit: TS within design_numbers.py tsband's band before; at least 0.03 V lower after the finger (an NTC, not a fixed 10k: DF-146); with 4.7k: CHG_STAT_N high within 2 s (paused); removed: CHG_STAT_N low again within 2 s; every unit
needs: 4.7k resistors and a clip-lead set (about $8, 2d)

procedure: python3 hardware/vv/tools/paper_checks.py ampstate (rewritten 2026-10-28 for 39cc07f): AMP_EN (IO45, module pin 26) held by R37 (100k, +1%) against the pad's leakage (1 uA, a stand-in 20 x IIH's 50 nA, esp32-s3.txt:3748), so Q3's gate against its 1.0 V minimum VGS(th) (2n7002_cj.txt:55); for each state (off with VSYS live, power-up before firmware, EN low, a watchdog or panic reset, sleep, USB in with the cell flat) the pad's reset state (GPIO45 WPD and IE at reset, esp32-s3.txt:901; no power-up glitch, Table 2-2, 958-1006); AMP_SHDN against VDD for VSYS 3.0-4.4 V with Q3's off leakage (1 uA stand-in; 80 nA at 60 V, 2n7002_cj.txt:57), against the 'supply voltage' the FM8002A names for shutdown (fm8002a.txt:75-76; it prints no VIH: limit 95% of VDD); U7's shutdown current (2 x its 4.2 uA typical, fm8002a.txt:123) and R36's added to the off budget (shelf, VER-103); --seed makes R37 100 Mohm and must fail
pass_limit: RESULT: PASS: U7 shut down in every state except the firmware driving AMP_EN high, for VSYS 3.0-4.4 V at every corner, with Q3's gate at least 0.4 V under its minimum VGS(th); U7's shutdown current and R36's together leave the off current within 30 uA (VER-65's limit); each threshold quoted from a datasheet with its line

title: Core values against rp2350.pdf's own rules (VREG, DVDD and IOVDD decoupling, crystal load, AVDD filter)
procedure: python3 hardware/vv/tools/paper_checks.py core: design.py's C24, C25, L2, R19, C26, X1, C27, C28, R21 and R22 against rp2350.pdf's component rules (rp2350.txt:33598-33612, 33281-33290, 40927-40950, 1196); then on the routed board (pcbnew) the capacitor nearest each DVDD, IOVDD, ADC_AVDD, USB_OTP_VDD and QSPI_IOVDD pin of U4, pad centre to pad centre: the two DVDD pins nearest VREG_LX want 100 nF close and the furthest 4.7 uF (rp2350.txt:32665-32675), ADC_AVDD and USB_OTP_VDD 100 nF close (32705, 32686); 'close' is read as 5 mm (Raspberry Pi's layout puts its 0402s 1-3 mm away); --seed makes C25 1 uF and must fail. The answer to VER-23's second-4.7 uF question from the datasheet itself, while RP-010329 is not on disk
pass_limit: RESULT: PASS: C24 >= 4.7 uF; C25 4.7 uF +-20%; L2 3.3 uH, the recommended AOTA-B201610S3R3-101-T; R19 and C26 33 ohm and 4.7 uF; X1 the ABM8-272-T3 with C27 and C28 giving CL 10 +-2.5 pF at 2-5 pF stray; R21 and R22 27 ohm; every DVDD, IOVDD, ADC_AVDD, USB_OTP_VDD and QSPI_IOVDD pin with a capacitor of the value the datasheet names within 5 mm (fails at 71737ae: DVDD pin 51's nearest +1V1 capacitor is C25 at 7.2 mm, C22 sits 15 mm away; DVDD pin 32, the furthest, has C21 100 nF and no 4.7 uF, C25 is 12 mm away; IOVDD pins 41 and 50 have none within 5 mm (the nearest at 7.4 and 6.7 mm), their own C17 and C15 sit about 10 mm away)
evidence: RETIRED in 39cc07f: the copied core's values left with the RP2354B; the module's supply and reset are VER-204's (was: FAIL at 5bedcef: three supply pins with no capacitor within 5 mm)

title: Application circuits and quoted constants for the ICs whose datasheets the script reads (U2, U3, U4, U8, U9, U11, the panel, J8's bus)

title: Clocked buses on paper: the panel's 8080 bus and the buttons' 24-bit shift-register chain against their datasheets' timing at the pad's drive and the load
procedure: python3 hardware/vv/tools/circuit_checks.py timing (rewritten 2026-10-28 for 39cc07f): each bus's track length from the routed board, its load (paper_checks.py's 0.1 pF/mm, an input and the FPC as stand-ins) and the module's pad (33 ohm, a stand-in: IOH 40 mA at VOH 2.64 V is the strongest drive, esp32-s3.txt:3752-3754) through R70-R78 and R65 give each edge; the 8080 write at 25 MHz (pinmap.md) against the ILI9488's parallel timing (twc 40 ns, twrh and twrl 15 ns, tdst and tdht 10 ns: ili9488.txt:16159-16172); SR_CLK to U8, U9 and U11 against the 74HC165's 2 V figures as the bound at 3.3 V (fmax, tw, tpd, SH/LD set-up, the input transition limit, SER hold over the clock's skew: sn74hc165.txt:264-265, 371-377, 472, 488, 503-504); the clock limits the firmware must keep are printed and must be written in docs/pinmap.md; --seed puts 1k in LCD_WR and must fail

title: The amplifier's heat on paper: U7 at its worst dissipation against its junction maximum
procedure: python3 hardware/vv/tools/thermal.py amp (rewritten 2026-10-28): U7 bridged into 8 ohm at VDD 4.5 V, its worst dissipation 2 VDD^2 / (pi^2 R) (a textbook result), in VER-144's air at 40 C outside; fm8002a.pdf (on disk since 2026-10-28) gives TJ 150 C (fm8002a.txt:112) and no thermal resistance, so a JEDEC SOIC-8's 160 C/W is the stand-in, printed; --seed doubles the theta and must fail
pass_limit: RESULT: PASS: U7's junction at or under 150 - 20 C at 40 C outside

title: The ESP32-S3 module's pins: functions, strapping pins at reset, power-up glitches, the PSRAM's pins (circuit_checks.py gpio)

title: The flex antenna's keep-out on the board and its clearance to metal (layout_checks.py antenna)
procedure: python3 hardware/vv/tools/layout_checks.py antenna (2026-10-28): the antenna's plate as docs/esp32s3_build.md places it on the case's left wall (x 64.5-71, y 62.1-107.9, a 40 mm U.FL cable); the board's 'antenna_keepout' rule area on both copper layers, forbidding tracks, vias, pours and footprints, and how much of the plate it covers; every track end, pad and pour vertex inside it; the plate's distance to the metal round it (the module's shield, the cell's pocket, the panel's glass outline from positions.json, J3, J8, the six M2 screws' bosses) against the 15 mm the design guidelines give for the module's own PCB antenna (esp32-s3-hw-design-guidelines.txt:1299), a stand-in until the flex antenna's maker's keep-out is on disk; --seed puts a pour vertex inside the keep-out and must fail

title: Wi-Fi range and throughput in the closed case on unit 1
procedure: unit 1 in its closed case with a cell, the antenna fitted on the left wall as assembly.md says: the module's RSSI from a 2.4 GHz access point at 1, 5 and 10 m line of sight with the device face up and face down, and an iperf-style TCP throughput at 10 m; the same with the antenna in free air off the board for comparison; record channel and TX power

title: 3V3 at the module through Wi-Fi TX bursts with the cell at the cutoff (bench)

title: The microSD card on unit 1: detect, 4-bit read and write, hot insertion with 3V3 on the scope
procedure: unit 1 on its cell: SD_CD reads low with a card in and high with none; the SDMMC host at 4 bits reads and writes 4 MB and compares (20 and 40 MHz); 20 insertions and removals while the panel and Wi-Fi run, with +3V3 at C11 on the scope (trigger on SD_CD); three card brands, their VDD capacitance measured with a meter first; JP6 cut to read the card's current with a DMM

title: Module identity logged per unit (chip, flash, PSRAM, MAC, eFuses)

pass_limit: ESP32-S3 with 16 MB flash and 8 MB PSRAM (the N16R8), 3.3 V VDD_SPI, no eFuse burnt but the factory's; one record per unit

title: The power key SW24 on unit 1: on, hold, off, 1 kohm in series, 1 Mohm across
procedure: the bench supply as the cell at 3.50 V, no USB: a 1 s press turns the device on and it stays on (PWR_HOLD set); a press under 1 s lets it fall off again; a long press turns it off; 1 kohm in series with SW24 (across its pads in place of a press) still turns it on and PWR_BTN_N reads low; then 1 Mohm across SW24's pads at 4.2 V for 10 min; then each unit's leakage across SW24 at 4.2 V
pass_limit: on, hold and off as pinmap.md's Power control says; with 1 kohm in series 3V3 >= 3.20 V within 50 ms; with 1 Mohm across, 3V3 < 0.5 V for 10 min; every unit's SW24 >= 100 Mohm

title: Flashing and recovery: USB Serial/JTAG with the case closed, the download mode through J7's pads
procedure: case closed: flash an image over USB-C (USB Serial/JTAG) and read its log; then an image that turns USB off: recover by holding BOOT (J7 pad 3) low through an EN pulse (J7 pad 2) on the pogo jig with the case open, powered from USB-C, never from J7's 3V3 pad with JP1 bridged (DF-189: J7's 3V3 back-feeds U3's OUT); time each recovery
pass_limit: flashes and logs over USB with the case closed; the download mode entered through J7 on 3 of 3 tries; the recovery's steps written into bringup.md
needs: a 4-pin 2.54 mm pogo jig (about $10, 7d)

title: The power key's printed cap: travel, force, nothing pressed face down
procedure: the printed pwr_cap in a printed seat-1 deck over a TPS850 on a board mock: calipers on the cap's rest height against case.scad (pwr_cap_top 0.5 under the face), the press to the switch's click (0.2 +0.1 mm travel, rocpu_tps850.txt:20) with a kitchen scale (250 +-50 gf, J14K, 33), and the case lying face down on a flat table and on a ridged surface with a 2 kg book on it
